## DAS-based upper bound

- b = 0.9849, **Sigma = −2.698**, **P(Mw ≥ 5.5)/yr = 0.07842**

This is the **upper bound, not calibrated**: DAS magnitudes are uncalibrated, and every one of the 62 detections is counted as an event at or above the catalogue magnitude of completeness Mc, so it **over-counts** events relative to the catalogue.

## Bottom line

The calibrated, catalogue-based estimate says a Pohang-like Mw ≥ 5.5 event at Brady Hot Springs in March 2016 is very unlikely — on the order of **10⁻⁴ per year** at b = 1.0 (≈5×10⁻⁶ over the observed volume), rising to ~1.5×10⁻² per year only at the low b = 0.65 scenario. The DAS-only number (7.8×10⁻² per year) is a conservative upper bound that inflates the count because uncalibrated DAS detections are treated as catalogue-complete events; the catalogue-based Sigma ≈ −5.3 to −5.4 (well below 0) indicates essentially no seismogenic response to the net-negative (extraction-dominated) operations during this window.
